entries.content:
Inkling 2 Mini from Thinking Machines is now available on AI Gateway. The small multimodal reasoning model is built for agentic coding, tool use, and knowledge work, with text and image inputs and text output.

Inkling 2 Mini has 26.4 billion total parameters and 3.4 billion active per token. The model runs its middle layers more than once for every token, which lets it reason further before writing anything down and often reach an answer with fewer reasoning tokens. Like Inkling 2 Small, it is strongest on long-running agentic tasks.

The model has a 1M-token context window, and reasoning effort can be set from 

none
through 
max
.

Use 

thinkingmachines/inkling-2-mini
as the model name: 
      
import { streamText } from 'ai';
const result = streamText({  model: 'thinkingmachines/inkling-2-mini',  prompt: 'Write a Python script that renames photos by the date they were taken.',});
for await (const text of result.textStream) {  process.stdout.write(text);}

To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup:

      
npx vercel ai-gateway setup

Then select 

thinkingmachines/inkling-2-mini
in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details.

Try Inkling 2 Mini in the model playground.

AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting, Zero Data Retention support, budgets for API keys, routing rules, and more.

AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests.

You can view all language models available on AI Gateway.

entries.title: AI Gateway now runs canary ZDR audits

entries.content:
AI Gateway now runs canary audits against inference providers to detect when prompt content is read outside the inference path.

Contractual Zero Data Retention (ZDR) agreements and point-in-time security audits establish how a provider should handle your data, but production infrastructure changes continuously. Canary audits add a detection layer on top.

Each canary audit run:

  1. Mints unique URLs that exist nowhere else, each mapped privately to a specific provider, model, and audit run.

  2. Sends prompts containing those URLs through the normal inference path, with ZDR requested for covered providers and non-ZDR pairs included as positive controls.

  3. Watches for traffic. A ZDR provider should never retain, inspect, or crawl prompt content, so a canary URL should never receive a request.

  4. Records any request to a canary URL, identifying the provider, model, and run for investigation.

Canary audits complement contractual ZDR agreements and independent audits rather than replacing them.

Read more about AI Gateway security and compliance measures in the documentation.

entries.content:
日本語版はこちら：Vercel日本法人の代表に花尾和成が就任いたしました

Kazunari Hanao has joined Vercel as Country Manager for Japan, based in Tokyo. His appointment is part of our continued investment in the Japanese market, including plans to expand our local team.

Japanese developers were early adopters of Next.js. And today, Vercel's customers in Japan include Mitsubishi Corporation, Fujitsu Limited, U-NEXT CO., Ltd., and DeNA Co., Ltd., alongside startups like SANU Inc. and Reiwa Travel, Inc.

Kazunari has spent the last decade building and leading software businesses in Japan. He joins Vercel from Pendo, where he was President of Pendo Japan. Before that, he built HashiCorp’s Japan business and spent nearly five years in sales leadership at Pivotal in Tokyo.

I asked him about the opportunity in Japan and his decision to join Vercel.

Copy link to headingWhy are you optimistic about Vercel's future in Japan?

Japan is at a turning point in how software gets built. The country has innovative companies and talented developers, but complex enterprise IT environments are slowing the adoption of frontier AI to the point that businesses can’t capture its value.

Vercel’s opportunity is to help Japanese enterprises move from experimentation to production, and run AI applications securely, reliably, and efficiently at scale. Cost, governance, and security for AI have become business priorities, not just technical ones. Almost every CXO I've met recently is working through those questions.

Copy link to headingWhat interested you in working for Vercel?

I've always been drawn to technology that simplifies complexity and helps businesses move faster. Vercel felt like a natural continuation of that, with bigger potential. AI is transforming the whole software development lifecycle, and Vercel has a real chance to become a foundational platform for the next generation of applications.

Ultimately what convinced me was the vision, the developer-first culture, and the chance to build something in Japan from the ground up. I enjoy building businesses, bringing talented people together, and creating an environment where teams feel empowered to take on hard problems. Vercel gives me the chance to do that with technology I believe in.

Copy link to headingWhat have you learned building businesses in Japan for global companies?

Building a successful business is about much more than growing revenue. It starts with bringing together the right people, uniting them around a shared goal, earning the trust of customers and partners, and building a culture where every team member feels ownership.

I've also learned how much it matters to connect global innovation with the specific needs of Japanese customers. During our first meetings, Guillermo and I talked about a future where countless digital services in Japan run on Vercel, and people experience its value every day whether they realize it or not. "Vercel Everywhere" is the future I want to build.

Copy link to headingWhat’s next in 2027

We're bringing our flagship conference, Ship, to Tokyo for the first time in 2027. It's a chance to hear directly from the Vercel team and from Japanese companies building on the platform. We'll share more details at vercel.com/ship in the new year.

We’re also growing our Tokyo team across sales, solutions engineering, and partnerships. A larger local team will help us support Japanese customers and deepen our partnerships with Classmethod, AWS Japan, and Sitecore Japan. Watch our careers page for upcoming opportunities in Japan.

entries.content:
（本記事は、英語版の就任発表の日本語訳に、花尾本人の就任のご挨拶を加えたものです。）

Vercel日本法人の代表に、花尾和成が就任いたしました（東京拠点）。今後、Vercelは花尾とともに国内のチームを拡充し、日本市場への投資をさらに進めていきます。

弊社が10年以上前に公開したNext.jsを、日本の開発者の皆さまはいち早く使い始めてくださいました。そして現在、日本では三菱商事、富士通、U-NEXT、ディー・エヌ・エーといった大企業から、SANUや令和トラベルといったスタートアップまで、幅広い企業にVercelをご利用いただいています。

花尾はこの10年間、日本でソフトウェア企業の運営にリーダーシップを発揮してきました。前職ではPendoの日本法人社長を務め、それ以前にはHashiCorpの日本事業を立ち上げ、Pivotalの東京オフィスで営業部門を統括しました。

就任にあたり、花尾から皆さまへのメッセージをご紹介します。

このたび、Vercelの日本法人代表に就任いたしました花尾和成です。私は20年以上IT業界に身を置き、そのうち10年以上は、開発者が開発そのものに集中できるようにするプロダクトに携わってまいりました。この経験を活かし、日本の開発者の皆さまと、その先にあるビジネスの価値を最大化することに貢献してまいります。

Vercelには、CEOのギシェルモ・ラウチを筆頭に、日本を好きなメンバーが数多くいます。こうした仲間の後押しを受けながら素晴らしいチームをつくり、Vercelが日本市場にとってかけがえのない存在となることを目指します。そして究極的には、直接的にも間接的にも、Vercelが日本のあらゆる場所で使われている世界を実現したいと考えています。

今後ともご指導ご鞭撻のほど、よろしくお願い申し上げます。

ここからは、私（Nick Bogaty, CRO）が聞き手を務めた花尾へのインタビューをお届けします。日本市場にどのような可能性を感じているのか、Vercelへの入社を決めた理由とあわせて伺いました。

Copy link to headingVercelが日本でさらに成長できるとお考えなのは、なぜですか？

日本のソフトウェア開発は、まさに転換期を迎えています。日本には革新的な企業が多く、高い技術力を持つ開発者の皆さまが活躍されています。一方で、多くの企業では既存のシステムが複雑になり、最先端のAIの導入がなかなか進んでいません。その結果、AIを十分に活用できていないケースもあります。

日本企業がAIのポテンシャルを引き出すには、AIを試す段階から本番運用へ進む必要があります。Vercelは、その一歩を後押しできると考えています。AIアプリケーションを大規模に、安全かつ安定して、効率よく運用できるよう支える。これはまさに、Vercelが強みを発揮できる領域です。

そして、AIにかかるコストをどう管理するか、どんなルールで運用するか、セキュリティをどう確保するか。いまやどれも技術部門だけでなく、経営陣にとっても優先課題です。最近お会いした経営幹部の方々も、こうした課題に取り組んでいると口をそろえておっしゃっていました。この点でも、Vercelは日本企業の力になれると考えています。

Copy link to headingVercelへの入社を決めた理由をお聞かせください。

複雑なことをシンプルにし、企業がもっとすばやく動けるようにする。以前から、そんなテクノロジーに魅力を感じてきました。Vercelなら、これまで私が取り組んできたことを、さらに大きな規模で実現できると思ったのです。いま、AIはソフトウェアの開発から運用まで、そのあり方を変えつつあります。そのなかで、Vercelは次世代のアプリケーションを支える基盤になれると考えています。

入社の決め手になったのは、Vercelのビジョンと、開発者の皆さまを第一に考える文化です。そして、日本で一から事業をつくっていけることにも惹かれました。私がやりがいを感じるのは、事業を立ち上げ、優れた人材を集め、チームが主体的に難しい課題に挑める環境をつくることです。Vercelでは、私自身が可能性を信じている技術を軸に、そうした仕事に取り組めると思いました。

Copy link to headingグローバル企業の日本事業を立ち上げるなかで、何を学ばれましたか？

事業を軌道に乗せるには、売上を伸ばすだけでは足りません。まずは仲間を集め、同じ目標に向かって力を合わせることが大切です。お客様やパートナー企業の信頼を得ることも欠かせません。そして、チームの一人ひとりが当事者意識を持ち、みずから動ける文化をつくること。そうした積み重ねが、事業の土台になります。

世界で生まれる新しい技術を、日本で暮らす方々が日々使うサービスに活かし、身近な課題の解決につなげることの大切さも学びました。CEOのギシェルモと出会った頃、日本で使われる数えきれないほどのデジタルサービスがVercel上で動く未来について語り合いました。Vercelの名前を知らない人にも、日々使うサービスを通じて、私たちの技術の価値が届く。私が実現したいのは、そんな「Vercel Everywhere」の未来です。

Copy link to heading2027年に向けた取り組み

2027年には、Vercelの代表的なカンファレンス「Ship」を初めて東京で開催します。Vercelの社員だけでなく、Vercelを活用してサービスを開発する日本企業の皆さまからも、それぞれの取り組みについて直接お聞きいただける機会となるよう準備を進めています。詳細は年明けにvercel.com/shipでお知らせいたします。

また、東京オフィスのチームも拡充します。営業、ソリューションエンジニアリング、パートナーシップの各分野で仲間を増やし、日本のお客様をより手厚くサポートできる体制をつくります。クラスメソッド、AWS Japan、Sitecore Japanといったパートナー企業との連携も、さらに深めていきます。日本での採用情報については、採用ページにて順次お知らせします。

entries.title: Introducing Audited ZDR on AI Gateway
entries.summary: AI is now used in every part of a business, and as a result, companies send source code, customer records, and regulated data through inference providers. entries.content:
AI is now used in every part of a business, and as a result, companies send source code, customer records, and regulated data through inference providers.

The assurance that no data is retained after processing is still publicly unverified. Payment platforms, cloud infrastructure, and most other layers that handle data this sensitive have a way to prove their controls to outside parties, and inference will follow the same path.

Today we are introducing Audited ZDR on AI Gateway. A provider is labeled Audited ZDR only after an independent security firm tests its zero data retention claims against its code, infrastructure, and live traffic, then publishes the report. Baseten, Modal, and Wafer are launch partners that have already begun audits, and more providers are encouraged to join to help raise the bar for security and privacy.

Audited ZDR builds on two steps we took toward stronger governance earlier this year:

  • We launched team-wide Zero Data Retention (ZDR) so teams could route traffic exclusively to providers stating a ZDR policy.

  • We completed our ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certification, which put Vercel’s own AI systems under independent third-party audit.

We are now asking inference providers for the same thing we asked of ourselves: independent verification.

Copy link to headingWhy a contract is not enough

ZDR guarantees rely on contracts and self-attestation. A provider agrees not to retain prompts or completions, and customers take that commitment on faith.

For teams sending proprietary code, customer information, or regulated data through models, self-reported ZDR contracts don't provide enough assurance.

  • Are prompts landing in debug logs, crash dumps, or tracing pipelines?

  • Can a rate limit push a request marked ZDR to a non-ZDR endpoint?

  • Can a support engineer's debugging tools surface a customer's prompt?

Answering these questions means running a bespoke security review for every provider and the models they host. An audit answers them in public.

Copy link to headingWhat Audited ZDR verifies

To qualify for Audited ZDR on AI Gateway, an inference provider engages an independent security firm, chosen from among respected third-party auditors, to run the audit. The firm then tests the provider's zero data retention policy across the serving path for every model, endpoint, feature, and tool that handles AI Gateway traffic.

The audit confirms that customer data is never written or retained on durable storage in any system. Customer data means prompts, completions, system prompts, embeddings, files, images and audio, tool and function-call payloads, and any derived data that could identify them. Coverage spans request logs, traces, metrics, crash dumps, prompt caches, abuse monitoring, analytics, backups, support tools, and training, fine-tuning, and evaluation datasets.

The audit confirms that once a response is returned to AI Gateway, that content is deleted from the inference provider's systems. Where a request uses caching, such as a KV cache, the cache must stay in volatile storage only for the period of the request, and never be written to durable storage. The audit requires this behavior to be disclosed.

The audit also confirms:

  • That a request marked ZDR never fails over to a non-ZDR endpoint, tool, or feature

  • That no human or automated process accesses customer data outside handling the request itself

  • That sub-processors with access comply with all of the above

  • That no training on customer data occurs

Auditors verify this by reviewing the inference provider's serving-path source code and infrastructure configuration, then running live tests. They send marked prompts through AI Gateway and search the provider's logging, caching, and storage systems for any trace of them.

Every passing provider publishes the report under the auditor's name. It covers scope, methodology, dates, findings, and fix status, with any exceptions disclosed and redactions limited to exploit detail. AI Gateway links directly to the report.

Copy link to headingCanary monitoring between audits

An independent audit checks a provider's code and infrastructure at a point in time, but production systems change. To add a detection layer between independent audits, Vercel also runs canary audits against inference providers on AI Gateway.

Each run sends prompts containing unique, unindexed URLs mapped privately to a provider, model, and run. Because a ZDR provider should never retain, inspect, or crawl prompt content, any request to a canary URL triggers an investigation into the provider and model involved. Canary checks cannot detect prompts written to disk and never read, so they complement independent code and infrastructure audits rather than replacing them.

Copy link to headingHow Audited ZDR works in AI Gateway

We are adding an independently Audited ZDR provider tier and a team-wide toggle in AI Gateway policy settings. When enabled, AI Gateway routes and fails over your team's requests only across providers with published audits that meet the bar.

Launch partners have started their audits, and each provider enters the tier as soon as its report is published. Launch partner reports are expected to be published by December 8, 2026.

Copy link to headingAbout AI Gateway

AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries and failover for higher uptime than connecting to providers directly. It reflects provider pricing with no markup and charges no platform fee on inference, including Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. Read the AI Gateway documentation to get started.

The audited tier works alongside AI Gateway's other compliance controls. Regional inference pins where a provider runs inference to the US, EU, Australia, or Japan, per request or team-wide, and any data the provider stores at rest stays in that region. If AI Gateway can't honor the region, the request fails rather than running elsewhere.

Provider headquarters filters routing by who owns the provider, so a request only reaches providers whose parent company is headquartered in a country you allow.

Private inference connects your own self-hosted or fine-tuned model endpoints to AI Gateway, called as 

private/
with the same SDKs, auth, and observability as catalog models and scoped to your team.

entries.title: AI Gateway now supports extraction models
entries.summary: Extraction models are now on AI Gateway. They find specific details in the content you provide, such as an invoice number or contact names, and return them as separate fields your code can use.ScaleDown Extract-1 is the first available extraction model. It extracts text values or lists of text values from text, images, and PDFs. You can use it to process invoices, contracts, and other records.Extr
entries.content:
Extraction models are now on AI Gateway. They find specific details in the content you provide, such as an invoice number or contact names, and return them as separate fields your code can use.

ScaleDown Extract-1 is the first available extraction model. It extracts text values or lists of text values from text, images, and PDFs. You can use it to process invoices, contracts, and other records.

Extraction is currently available through the AI SDK only. With 

ai@7.0.176
or later, use 
experimental_extract
and the model ID 
scaledown/extract-1
: 
      
import { experimental_extract as extract } from 'ai';
const result = await extract({  model: 'scaledown/extract-1',  state: 'Invoice INV-2041 from Acme Corp. Contacts: Ana, Bo.',  fields: {    invoiceNumber: { type: 'text', instructions: 'The invoice number' },    contacts: { type: 'list', items: 'text', instructions: 'Contact names' },  },});
console.log(result.answers.invoiceNumber.value); // 'INV-2041'console.log(result.answers.contacts.value); // ['Ana', 'Bo']

Extract an invoice number and contact names from text.

Each key in 

fields
has an entry in 
result.answers
. If a field is not found, its 
value
is 
null
. Extract-1 returns confidence scores from 0 to 1 for matches, including individual list items, so you can flag uncertain results for review. For text input, it can also return character offsets showing where a match appears.

To extract from a PDF or image, pass it as a file part in 

state
: 
      
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';import { experimental_extract as extract } from 'ai';
const result = await extract({  model: 'scaledown/extract-1',  state: [    {      type: 'file',      data: await readFile('./invoice.pdf'),      mediaType: 'application/pdf',    },  ],  fields: {    vendor: { type: 'text', instructions: 'The company that issued the invoice' },    total: { type: 'text', instructions: 'The total amount due' },    lineItems: { type: 'list', items: 'text', instructions: 'The line items' },  },});
console.log(result.answers);

Extract the vendor, total, and line items from a PDF.

Extraction requests appear in AI Gateway logs and spend tracking. See the extraction quickstart for setup and authentication.

entries.title: Vercel Drives adds CLI commands and standalone SDKs
entries.summary: You can now create, list, fork, and delete Vercel Drives with the new vercel drives commands or standalone SDKs for TypeScript (@vercel/drives) and Python (vercel-drives). Drives also have a REST API at /v1/drives and Drive-specific permissions, so managing them no longer requires Sandbox APIs or permissions.With the latest Vercel CLI, link your project with vercel link if needed, then run:Install
entries.content:
You can now create, list, fork, and delete Vercel Drives with the new 

vercel drives
commands or standalone SDKs for TypeScript (
@vercel/drives
) and Python (
vercel-drives
). Drives also have a REST API at 
/v1/drives
and Drive-specific permissions, so managing them no longer requires Sandbox APIs or permissions.

With the latest Vercel CLI, link your project with 

vercel link
if needed, then run: 
      
vercel drives get-or-create workspace-cache --region iad1vercel drives listvercel drives fork existing-drive existing-drive-fork

Create, list, and fork Drives with the Vercel CLI.

Install the TypeScript SDK with 

npm install @vercel/drives
, or the Python SDK with 
pip install vercel-drives
, then run: 
      
import { Drive } from '@vercel/drives';
await Drive.getOrCreate({  name: 'workspace-cache',  region: 'iad1',});
const driveList = await Drive.list();for await (const item of driveList) {  console.log(item.name);}
const source = await Drive.get({ name: 'existing-drive' });const fork = await source.fork({ name: 'existing-drive-fork' });console.log(fork.name);

Create, list, and fork Drives with the TypeScript SDK.

Drives still mount into Vercel Sandboxes as before, and existing Sandbox CLI commands and SDK code continue to work. Drives also now have their own pages in the Vercel dashboard and Observability.

Drives are available on Hobby, Pro, and Enterprise plans. Learn more in the Drives documentation.

entries.title: Catch missing feature flags before they reach production
entries.summary: Vercel Flags can now block a deployment from reaching production if you’ve declared a flag in code but haven’t created it in your project. Without that definition, your app can silently fall back to the flag’s default value, even if that turns on a feature you meant to keep off.The Flag Definitions Present Deployment Check runs when a deployment is ready. If any flags are missing, the check fails
entries.content:
Vercel Flags can now block a deployment from reaching production if you’ve declared a flag in code but haven’t created it in your project. Without that definition, your app can silently fall back to the flag’s default value, even if that turns on a feature you meant to keep off.

The Flag Definitions Present Deployment Check runs when a deployment is ready. If any flags are missing, the check fails and lists them in the results, where you can create each one before redeploying.

The check reads your Flags SDK discovery endpoint. With 

flags@4.5.0
or later on Vercel, it works without 
FLAGS_SECRET
; earlier versions still require the secret.

To turn on blocking, teams on all plans can enable the check in their project’s Build and Deployment settings and mark it as required. See the Deployment Checks documentation for setup details.

AI Gateway skips providers in blocked countries and routes requests to the r
entries.content:
Provider headquarters sends your AI Gateway requests only to providers headquartered in countries you choose, so you can meet compliance and procurement rules about where your AI vendors are located.

You can configure provider headquarters to be an allowlist of the countries to use, or a denylist of the countries to block. AI Gateway skips providers in blocked countries and routes requests to the rest of the list, so a model stays accessible as long as it is available in one of its allowed provider locations.

Use provider headquarters with regional hosting and regional inference to control where a request is received, where the model runs, and who runs it.

Copy link to headingSet provider headquarters for your team

Pro and Enterprise customers can apply their provider headquarters list to every AI Gateway request across their team. Configure the list in AI Gateway settings.

Provider headquarters settings are applied automatically as AI Gateway adds models and providers. Providers without a headquarters country on record never receive your requests.

Copy link to headingSet provider headquarters per request

On any plan, set 

headquarters
in the gateway provider options to restrict a single request. Pass country codes for an allowlist, or prefix every code with 
!
for a denylist, as in 
['!US']
. If your team has a list, a request can only narrow it.

In the examples below, requests are only sent to providers based in the US and Germany:

      
import { generateText } from 'ai';
const { text } = await generateText({  model: 'openai/gpt-oss-120b',  prompt: 'Explain HTTP caching in one sentence.',  providerOptions: {    gateway: {      headquarters: ['US', 'DE'],    },  },});
console.log(text);

Both settings filter providers, so a model stays available as long as one of its providers is based in an allowed country. If no provider is available in an allowed country, AI Gateway tries your fallback models. If no fallback models are available in allowed countries, or if no fallback models are configured, the request will fail without trying to route to providers in other locations.

Read the provider headquarters documentation for the countries supported, pricing and setup details.

entries.content:
Vercel Functions now accept inbound request bodies up to 20MiB, up from 4.5MB, in Public Beta.

To turn this on, set the 

VERCEL_SUPPORT_LARGE_REQUEST_BODY=1
environment variable. The opt-in applies to the whole project in the environment where you set it, so you can test the larger limit on preview before enabling it in production. It requires the project's functions to use the performance memory setting of 4GB. It applies to functions on the Node.js, Python, and Bun runtimes, and to Routing Middleware. Functions and Routing Middleware on the Edge runtime keep the 4.5MB cap and return 413 on oversize bodies, so moving them onto the larger limit means switching to the Node.js runtime with 
runtime: 'nodejs'
, or 
proxy.ts
in Next.js.

When a project opts in, Routing Middleware receives request headers and metadata but no request body, enforced at the project level. Middleware still runs and still sees every other request header, so body-dependent middleware behavior is the one thing that becomes unavailable. This avoids sending the body twice, to both middleware and the target function, which would raise cost and time to first byte.

When handling larger request bodies, read the body promptly and avoid holding it in memory to prevent backpressure and memory issues.

Learn more in the Vercel Functions limitations documentation.
